title: Versioning prompts and tracking the effect of each change

videos.script: So far every version of the prompt has had a file of its own. A prompt in production lives in one file, and its past lives in git. {{log}} This lesson reads that past. Eight commits over two weeks of August, each with a line saying what changed. {{diff}} First you work out what a version actually is. The text is part of it. So are the settings, the model and the messages you judged it by. Change one of them and the score moves, even when the file does not. {{hot}} Then you run every commit against the same forty messages. One command prints a score and a token count for each. {{score}} Most of the history is quiet. Two commits cost tokens and moved nothing. And one, called make the examples easier to read, took the score from thirty-six to zero. {{zero}} It stayed in the file for three days. By the end of the lesson you can see a change like that the same afternoon, before it is merged, with the names of the messages it broke. {{close}}
